items.text: In adults after primary total knee replacement, does wearable-based activity feedback during the first 12 weeks, compared with usual rehabilitation, improve patient-reported function at about three months?
items.population: Adults after primary total knee replacement
items.intervention: Wearable activity tracker with feedback (targets, app messages or physiotherapist messages) for up to 12 weeks
items.comparator: Usual rehabilitation, or the device without feedback
items.outcome: Patient-reported knee function at 10 to 14 weeks

items.text: What do patients recovering from knee replacement experience when using activity feedback, and what makes them stop?
items.population: Adults using activity feedback after knee replacement
items.intervention: Experience of wearing a tracker and receiving feedback
items.outcome: Reasons for continued use or stopping, including technology access and step targets

finer: Feasible in eight weeks with the confirmed library hours; interesting to the committee and the physiotherapy team; novel only as an update focused on function and older patients; ethical as a review of published data; relevant because a lease decision is scheduled.
summary: One PICO effectiveness question and one SPIDER question on experience and stopping.
